article.title: How the media sold the Iraq War – and it’s doing it again on Iran
article.author: Zoe Alexandra
article.content: Iraq had “WMDs.” Now Iran has a “dirty bomb.” As CNN amplifies anonymous claims that Iran is plotting an attack on DC, BT Live’s Zoe Alexandra rewinds the tape on the corporate media blitz that sold us the Iraq War – from Colin Powell’s 2003 UN presentation on Saddam Hussein to the mainstream reporting that turned fake intelligence into an invasion. The playbook’s the same, and so is the goal: making a deeply unpopular war look necessary. Now Trump’s warning Iran is “looking at gases, looking at bio,” even as CNN’s own reporter admits the intel doesn’t indicate an imminent attack, and the White House concedes it knows of no credible threat. Tehran calls the reporting “a coordinated, malign narrative campaign” – and it comes just weeks after midterm voters routed Republicans over an Iran war most Americans oppose. But Democrats are promptly falling in line: André Carson told CNN that Iran is “losing their grip,” and Hakeem Jeffries ruled out using the December budget fight to defund the war, betting instead on a war powers resolution that Trump is all but certain to veto. Eight months into one of the most unpopular wars in US history, Zoe asks who benefits from the US media manufacturing consent for more.
